course_name_original: Production Systems Engineering - Ingineria sistemelor de producție

learning_outcomes.text: Systemic acquisition of basic knowledge in the field of the life cycle of complex engineering process systems, with reference to design and integration needs of processes and environmental implications.
Familiarization with terminology, methods, and typical specific concepts, targeting component elements, structuring, functioning, calculation, and model conditions.
Acquisition of methods for analysis and optimization of industrial manufacturing processes.
Evaluation of projects by applying life cycle precepts.

syllabus_topics: Concept of systems engineering and process engineering. Typology of process systems
Methods of analysis in process systems engineering
Models and meta-models in process systems engineering
Analysis and evaluation of processes in process systems engineering
Specific activities in process systems engineering
Product life cycle and associated costs
Structural-functional analysis of modular numerically controlled technological equipment
CAD-CAM methods for designing 3-axis milling processes
Establishing cutting regime parameters for milling and their influence on the roughness of machined surfaces
Analysis of workpiece installation devices. Determination of clamping forces developed by machine vises
Comparative study of milling strategies for complex geometric entities
Computer-aided technological design of 2½-axis and 4-axis milling processes
Analysis of computer-aided ultrasonic welding technologies for plastics and composites
teaching_methods: Study of curricular documents and bibliography

assessment_methods.method: Course evaluation (understanding, knowledge accumulation, method application) via 3 distributed checks and a written examination
Summative evaluation of applied activities (applied assignment and presentation of laboratory reports)

assessment_rules: The course's theoretical part is evaluated through three distributed checks and a written examination, which also test the ability to use methods in applications. Applied activities are assessed via a summative evaluation consisting of an applied assignment and presentation of laboratory reports with processing and interpretation of experimental results. A bonus is awarded for 66% course attendance. Minimum performance requires knowing and applying a method for designing/optimizing manufacturing processes, evaluating a project based on its life cycle, and evaluating quality, verified through applications based on analysis of stages and results.
